explanation: Charging a capacitor through a resistor, its voltage rises along V(t) = V0(1 - e^(-t/RC)), reaching about 63% of V0 after one time constant tau = RC. The energy it banks is U = 1/2·C·V^2 — note the SQUARE, so the last volts store far more energy than the first. Slide C, V0, and R: bigger C or V0 fills the green energy bar higher, while bigger R (or C) stretches tau so it charges more slowly. The curve resets and recharges so you can watch the whole rise repeatedly.
bullets: Stored energy U = 1/2 C V^2 grows with the SQUARE of voltage — doubling V quadruples U.
Charge follows Q = C·V; on the curve V reaches ~63% of V0 after one time constant tau = RC.
Larger R or C lengthens tau (slower charging); the final energy depends only on C and V0.
